headline: Approved condo expansion at 78 Amherst Street, vehicle repair permit at 444 Amherst Street, and self-storage site plan at 111 Northeastern Boulevard.
summary: The board approved a site plan and conditional use permit for two duplexes totaling 10 condo units at 3-13 Putnam Street and 78 Amherst Street, approved a conditional use permit for a vehicle repair business at 444 Amherst Street, and approved a parking waiver and site plan for added self-storage containers at 111 Northeastern Boulevard. The board also amended a condition on a conditional use permit at 310 Daniel Webster Highway and postponed applications for 8 Merrit Parkway and 66 Concord St to the October 1, 2026 meeting. Subdivision applications for 78 Amherst Street and 8 Blue Hill Ave were withdrawn.
decisions: Postponed application A26-0166 for 8 Merrit Parkway to the October 1, 2026 meeting.
Postponed application A26-0167 for 66 Concord St to the October 1, 2026 meeting.
Withdrew subdivision plan application A26-0153 for 78 Amherst St.
Withdrew subdivision plan application A26-0160 for 8 Blue Hill Ave.
Withdrew condominium subdivision application A26-0154 for 3-13 Putnam Street & 78 Amherst Street.
Approved three waivers for Site Plan A26-0153 at 3-13 Putnam Street & 78 Amherst Street, 6-0.
Approved Conditional Use Permit A26-0178 for 3-13 Putnam Street & 78 Amherst Street, 6-0.
Approved Site Plan A26-0153 for 3-13 Putnam Street & 78 Amherst Street with multiple conditions, 6-0.
Approved a modification of Conditional Use Permit A26-0170 for 310 Daniel Webster Highway, amending Condition #1, 6-0.
Approved a waiver to not submit a site plan for Conditional Use Permit A26-0164 at 444 Amherst Street, 6-0.
Approved Conditional Use Permit A26-0164 for a vehicle repair business at 444 Amherst Street, 6-0, with a condition.
Approved a parking waiver allowing 15 spaces where 50 are required for Site Plan A26-0186 at 111 Northeastern Boulevard, 6-0.
Approved Site Plan A26-0186 for self-storage containers at 111 Northeastern Boulevard, 6-0, with conditions.

EXPANDED DRAFT MEETING SUMMARY 
THIS IS NOT AN OFFICIAL TRANSCRIPT OF TAPE RECORDED PROCEEDINGS 
THE INFORMATION CONTAINED HEREIN HAS NOT BEEN REVIEWED OR APPROVED BY THE NCPB 
 
NASHUA CITY PLANNING BOARD 
September 17, 2026 
 
The regularly scheduled meeting of the Nashua City Planning Board 
was held on September 17, 2026 at 7:00PM in the 3rd floor auditorium 
in City Hall. 
 
Members Present: Joe MacIntyre, Mayor’s Representative 
 Adam Varley, Vice Chair 
 Cameron Green, Clerk 
 Dan Hudson, City Engineer 
 Ald. Patricia Klee 
 Larry Hirsch 
   
  
Also Present: Sam Durfee, Planning Manager 
 Connor Muise, Deputy Planning Manager 
 Scott McPhie, Planner I 
  
APPROVAL OF MINUTES 
 
September 3, 2026 
 
MOTION by Mr. MacIntyre to approve the minutes, as amended. 
 
SECONDED by Ald. Klee 
 
MOTION CARRIED 4-0-2 (Hirsch, Green abstained) 
 
COMMUNICATIONS 
 
- A26-0166, 8 Merrit Parkway 
o Postponed to the 10/1/26 meeting 
- A26-0167, 66 Concord St 
o Postponed to the 10/1/26 meeting 
- A26-0164, 444 Amherst St 
o Revised CUP letter 
- A26-0186, 111 Northeastern Blvd 
o Revised staff report 
- A26-0153, 78 Amherst St Subdivision Plan 
o Withdrawn 
- A26-0160, 8 Blue Hill Ave Subdivision Plan 
o Withdrawn
NCPB 
September 17, 2026 
Page 2 
 
REPORT OF CHAIR, COMMITTEE, & LIAISON 
 
None 
 
PROCEDURES OF THE MEETING 
 
After the legal notice of each conditional, speci al use permit, 
site plan or subdivision plan is read by the Chair, the Board will 
determine if that the application is complete and ready for the 
Board to take jurisdiction. The public hearing will begin at which 
time the applicant or representative will be given time to present 
an overview and description of their project. The applicant shall 
speak to whether or not they agree with recommended staff 
stipulations. The Board will then have an opportunity to ask 
questions of the applicant or staff. 
 
The Chair will then ask for testimony from the audience. First 
anyone wishing to speak in opposition or with concern to the plan 
may speak. Please come forward to the microphone, state their name 
and address for the record. This would be the time to ask questions 
they may have regarding the plan. Next public testimony will come 
from anyone wishing to speak in favor of the plan. The applicant 
will then be allowed a rebuttal period at which time they shall 
speak to any issues or concerns raised by prior public testimony. 
 
One public member will then be granted an opportunity to speak to 
those issues brought by the applicant during their rebuttal period. 
The Board will then ask any relevant follow -up questions of the 
applicant if need be. 
 
After this is completed the public hearing will end and the Board 
will resume the public meeting at which time the Board will 
deliberate and vote on the application before us. The Board asks 
that both sides keep their remarks to the subject at hand and try 
not to repeat what has already been said. 
 
Above all, the Board wants to be fair to everyone and make the 
best possible decision based on the testimony presented and all 
applicable approval criteria established in the Nashua Revised 
Ordinances for conditional, special use permits, sit e plans and 
subdivisions. Thank you for your interest and courteous attention. 
Please turn off your cell phones and pagers at this time. 
 
Per our legal charter, we have a quorum when five members are 
present. There may be some recusals this evening for certain board 
members, but as long as five members are sitting each case can be
NCPB 
September 17, 2026 
Page 3 
 
heard. At the discretion of the chair, the order of the cases can 
be rearranged.  
 
NEW BUSINESS – CONDITIONAL USE PERMITS 
A26-0178  78 Amherst Street, LLC (Owner), Family Realty 
Investments, LLC (Owner & Applicant) requesting site 
plan and conditional use permit approval to merge both 
lots and construct two duplexes, for a total of ten 
condominium units on one lot. Property is located at 3-
13 Putnam Street & 78 Amherst Street. Map 62 – Lots 83 
& 85. Zoned B Urban Residence (R-B). Ward 2. 
 
NEW BUSINESS – SUBDIVISION PLANS 
A26-0154  78 Amherst Street, LLC (Owner), Family Realty 
Investments, LLC (Owner & Applicant) requesting site 
plan and condominium subdivision approval to merge both 
lots and construct two duplexes, for a total of ten 
condominium units on one lot. Property is located at 3-
13 Putnam Street & 78 Amherst Street. Map 62 – Lots 83 
& 85. Zoned B Urban Residence (R-B). Ward 2. (Withdrawn) 
 
NEW BUSINESS – SITE PLANS 
A26-0153  78 Amherst Street, LLC (Owner), Family Realty 
Investments, LLC (Owner & Applicant) requesting site 
plan and condominium subdivision approval to merge both 
lots and construct two duplexes, for a total of ten 
condominium units on one lot. Property is located at 3-
13 Putnam Street & 78 Amherst Street. Map 62 – Lots 83 
& 85. Zoned B Urban Residence (R-B). Ward 2. (Postponed 
to the September 17, 2026 meeting) 
 
Mr. Varley said he would take A26-0153 and A26-0178 together. 
 
MOTION by Mr. Green that the applicatio ns are complete and the 
Planning Board is ready to take jurisdiction 
 
SECONDED by Mr. Hudson 
 
MOTION CARRIED 6-0 
 
Paul Chisholm, Civil Engineer, Keach Nordstrom Associates, 5 
Commerce Park N Ste 201, Bedford, NH
NCPB 
September 17, 2026 
Page 4 
 
Mr. Chisholm introduced himself on behalf o f the owner. The plan 
before you tonight is an expansion to Putnam Place, Phase II. The 
existing condominium at 3 -13 Putnam Street is six units; the 
proposal is to expand that to ten. The project requires a 
conditional use permit to expand that use in the RB zone.  We plan 
to raze the derelict single -family home at 78 Amherst St and 
construct two new duplexes. The four new units will face Amherst 
Street. The parking will be oriented in the same direction as it 
currently is, it will just be expanded up towar d Amherst Street. 
The driveway for 78 Amherst Street will be removed.  
 
Mr. Chisholm outlined topography, lighting, and landscaping. There 
will be a 6-ft high stockade fence, a couple of arborvitaes, and 
some additional plantings to screen the property. He described the 
stormwater improvements, proposed architecture, and deck design. 
 
Mr. Chisholm said this project requires a conditional use permit 
to expand the multifamily use. We believe this is a compatible and 
logical expansion to an existing developmen t that will provide 
continuity to the area. It will not substantially change the 
character of the property and will make productive use of a parcel 
that is somewhat constrained. We are requesting three waivers, as 
detailed in the staff report. We have received staff comments, we 
haven’t had a chance to address all of them but we see none that 
stand in the way with this project. We feel comfortable with the 
conditions proposed. We take no exceptions to the conditions 
proposed in the staff report. We feel thi s is a reasonable 
expansion, fits in the neighborhood, and provides continuity  to 
the property. 
 
Mr. Varley asked if the electrical connection to the existing units 
is overhead.  
 
Mr. Chisholm said yes.  
 
Ald. Klee asked how many additional units there will be. 
 
Mr. Chisholm said there are six currently, and there will be four 
more. Two and two.  
 
Ald. Klee asked where the fence and arborvitae will be located.  
 
Mr. Chisholm said it’s in between the edge of the parking area and 
Amherst Street.  
 
Ald. Klee asked if it goes to the corner of Putnam.
NCPB 
September 17, 2026 
Page 5 
 
 
Mr. Chisholm said yes.  
 
Ald. Klee asked if the current parking lot entrance will remain.  
 
Mr. Chisholm said correct. There is a driveway for the house, and 
that will be removed.  
 
SPEAKING IN OPPOSITION OR CONCERN 
 
None 
 
SPEAKING IN FAVOR 
 
None 
 
Mr. MacIntyre said there are six units on .67 acres, and we’re 
adding another four. On a site that small, is this in spirit with 
the Master Plan? 
 
Mr. Durfee said from the context of more building and lot coverage 
perspective, it’s within keeping of the regulations. The Master 
Plan doesn’t get so granular as to dictate those lot coverage 
regulations. More broadly speaking, adding housing is a master 
plan goal. This is in keeping with that goal.  
 
Mr. MacIntyre said this is a small project. What do the regulations 
state for density of units? 
 
Mr. Durfee said maximum density is 7 units per acre, and what is 
proposed is almost 15 units per acre. This did receive a density 
variance from the Zoning Board on April 14, 2026.   
 
Mr. MacIntyre said he agrees with the aesthetics of razing the 
home, that’s a good move.  
 
Ald. Klee asked if the staff report refers to capping the old sewer 
line, and a new one will be brought into the site.  
 
Mr. Hudson said yes, the sewer service is to th e existing house. 
They will be tying into the sewer on the condo lot, they won’t 
need a new line. That whole site will share the same service. 
 
Ald. Klee asked if that line can handle all the units.
NCPB 
September 17, 2026 
Page 6 
 
Mr. Hudson said we believe so. We’ve asked them to subm it 
calculations. 
 
Ald. Klee asked if the applicant concurs.  
 
Mr. Chisholm said correct. Given minimum sizes of sewer pipes, 
they can handle quite a bit of flow compared to what this 
development will create. I can submit the calculations, and if 
there are any improvements that need to be done his client will do 
what he has to do.  
 
PUBLIC MEETING 
 
Mr. Varley closed the public hearing and opened the public meeting. 
He said this is an improvement over what is there. It’s a fairly 
modest expansion. Increased density meets the housing goal of the 
Master Plan.  
 
Ald. Klee said when we had review by an outside consultant they 
advised that we should be building to what the neighborhood is. 
She feels that this property is not consistent with the 
neighborhood. She wo n’t not vote for this, but we need to keep 
looking at this to not change the character of old neighborhoods.  
 
Mr. MacIntyre said he agrees with Ald. Klee, this sticks out in 
the neighborhood. His real concern was to clarify how much we’re 
going to jam pack on a small lot. This is pushing it. If it’s 
within regulation, he’ll go with it. This is so close to being too 
much on too little.  
 
Mr. Green said he used to share a window with this lot and was 
there for the construction of the original six units. The way that 
the site is laid out, these last four units make it a much better 
plan. It completes the Amherst Street portion.  
 
Ald. Klee said if it weren’t for the fact that those apartments to 
the north exist, she doesn’t think she could vote f or this. She 
would want a different look to the façade. They’re not 
unattractive, but it’s not in keeping with the neighborhood. The 
rezoning effort is to keep neighborhoods similar.  
 
Mr. Green said this is a natural ending stop on Amherst Street 
before it continues into more a residential feeling. Otherwise it 
would be very out of place.
NCPB 
September 17, 2026 
Page 7 
 
MOTION by Mr. Green to approve the following waivers for New 
Business – Site Plan A26-0153: 
 
a. §190-279 EE: to waive the requirement to show all existing 
features on adjacent parcels.  
 
b. §190-221: to waive the requirement to install all utilities 
underground.  
 
c. §190-198: to waive the requirement to exceed the maximum 
number of parking spaces. 
 
As per RSA 674:36(II)(N), RSA 674:44(III)(e), and §190 -148(D), 
Strict conformity would pose an unnecessary hardship to the 
Applicant and the waiver would not be contrary to the spirit and 
intent of the regulations; and specific circumstances, or 
conditions of the land, and the waiver will properly carry out the 
spirit and intent of the regulations. 
 
SECONDED by Ald. Klee 
 
MOTION CARRIED 6-0 
 
MOTION by Mr. Green to approve New Business – Conditional Use 
Permit A26-0178. The Board finds that the application meets the 
Approval Criteria under §190-133(F). 
 
SECONDED by Ald. Klee 
 
MOTION CARRIED 6-0 
 
MOTION by Mr. Green to approve New Business – Site Plan A26-0153. 
The Board finds that the application meets the Approval Criteria 
under §190-146(D) with the following conditions: 
 
a. All Technical Review Comments in the Planning Staff report 
shall b e addressed to the satisfaction of the Planning 
Department.  
 
b. Any waiver(s) granted shall be listed on the plan. Should any 
waiver(s) be denied, the plan must be revised to comply with 
the applicable site plan regulations.  
 
c. All conditions from the Planning Board decision letter will 
be added to the plan.
NCPB 
September 17, 2026 
Page 8 
 
d. All outstanding comments in a memorandum from Joe Mendola, 
PE, Senior Staff Engineer, dated August 27, 2026, shall be 
addressed to the satisfaction of the Division of Public Works.  
 
e. Per the Fire Marshal’s Office, the four new condominium units 
will be as numbered Amherst Street addresses, with the sub -
addresses as follows:  
 
a. Proposed 78  
b.  Proposed 80A  
c. Proposed 80B  
d. Proposed 82A  
e. Proposed 82B  
 
f. Prior to the issuance of a building permit, the change in 
addressing from 78 Amherst Street to 78, 80 A& B, & 82 A& B 
Amherst Street shall be approved by the Board of Aldermen.  
 
g. The lot line merger form will be completed and placed on file 
at the registry of deeds at the applicant's expense.  
 
h. As this is an identi fied inactive asbestos site, all work 
must comply with Chapter Env -Sw 2100 and Env -A 1800 of the 
New Hampshire Code of Administrative Rules.  
 
i. Prior to the issuance of a Building Permit, the Condominium 
Site Plan shall be recorded at the Registry of Deeds, at the 
Applicant’s expense. The Applicant shall provide the City 
with checks for the necessary recording fees.  
 
j. All proposed demolition activities require inspections for 
the presence of asbestos containing materials prior to 
Environmental Health’s sign-off on Nashua’s Building Safety 
Department’s Demolition Permit Approval Form.  
 
k. Prior to the commencement of site work, a pre -construction 
meeting shall be held, and a financial guarantee, to be 
reviewed and approved by City staff, shall be in place.  
 
l. Four-months prior to the first request for a Certificate of 
Occupancy, the Applicant shall provide the Planning 
Department with a draft of the Declaration of Condominium 
documents for review and comment.
NCPB 
September 17, 2026 
Page 9 
 
m. Prior to the issuance of a Certificate of Occupancy, all 
stormwater documents shall be updated and recorded to reflect 
the four additional units.  
 
n. Prior to the issuance of a Certificate of Occupancy, all site 
improvements will be completed.  
 
o. Prior to the issuance of the final Certificate of Occupancy, 
an a s-built plan locating all driveways, buildings, 
utilities, and site landscaping shall be completed by a 
professional engineer or a licensed land surveyor and 
submitted to the Engineering and Planning Departments. The 
as-built plan shall include a statement that all construction 
was completed in accordance with the approved site plan and 
applicable local regulations.  
 
p. Prior to the issuance of a Certificate of Occupancy, school 
impact fees shall be paid, in accordance with Article VIII 
Impact Fees of the Nashua Land Use Code. 
 
SECONDED by Ald. Klee 
 
MOTION CARRIED 6-0 
 
NEW BUSINESS – CONDITIONAL USE PERMITS 
A26-0170  EC NH Real Estate Holdings (Owner & Applicant) 
requesting a modification of condition #1 of a 
Conditional Use Permit approved on September 7th, 2023 
and amended on September 5th, 2024, and December 11th, 
2025. Property is located at 310 Daniel Webster Highway. 
Map A – Lot 733. Zoned General Business (GB). Ward 7. 
 
MOTION by Mr. Green that the application is complete and the 
Planning Board is ready to take jurisdiction 
 
SECONDED by Mr. MacIntyre 
 
MOTION CARRIED 6-0 
 
Atty. Morgan Hollis, Gottesman & Hollis PA, 39 East Pearl St, 
Nashua NH 
 
Atty. Hollis introduced himself on behalf of the owner. He said 
this is his third time back for an extension, and  he apologizes 
for that. We have improvements that are being made to the Zimmerman 
Board and Ski site, which we have finally reached agreement on.
NCPB 
September 17, 2026 
Page 10 
 
Now we can move to the other three players: Macy’s, Target, and 
Simon Malls. This has been a complicated and fluid situation in 
that there are a lot of improvement benefitting the Zimmerman 
parcel, which will affect the other parcels. Everyone has engaged 
their own lawyer and their own development vice president and 
they’ve changed over the years. We have a signe d agreement with 
Zimmerman, and that will advance the ball significantly. Someone 
has to blink first, and we reached an agreement this week. We are 
optimistic we will have this done by the timeframe asked.  
 
SPEAKING IN OPPOSITION OR CONCERN 
 
None 
 
SPEAKING IN FAVOR 
 
None 
 
Mr. Hudson said he appreciates the continued effort by the 
applicant. It is complicated, if it was easy it would be done by 
now. He feels that we are close.  
 
Ald. Klee said she voted against thi s originally because there 
were a lot of specific issues, especially with the intersection. 
She respects the fact that the applicant has kept Mr. Hudson 
involved. She is for this extension because she believes they are 
doing all the right things.  
 
Mr. MacIntyre s aid he appreciates the effort to keep the ball 
rolling. He asked staff if this drags into August 2027, that any 
activity going on at the Sheraton hotel would be going on at the 
same time.  
 
Mr. Durfee said it’s possible, but we’re pretty far away from 
actually finalizing things with the Sheraton hotel. What the Board 
approved was concept plans, the NHDOT has to approve them too. 
That project was appealed to Superior Court, so it’s a big unknown. 
 
Mr. MacIntyre asked he doesn’t want activity at two locations  at 
the same time.  
 
Mr. Hudson said if the two happen concurrently it’s not a bad 
situation necessarily. The work here is specifically for 
Zimmermans driveway access configuration, it has a very small 
focus. He doesn’t see an issue.
NCPB 
September 17, 2026 
Page 11 
 
PUBLIC MEETING 
 
Mr. Varley closed the public hearing and opened the public meeting. 
He said it’s apparent that the applicant wants to get this done 
and is making all efforts to do that. He is in favor.  
 
Ald. Klee said she echoes Mr. Varley’s sentiments. There has been 
activity, granting this extension is in keeping with moving this 
forward. We should approve this.  
 
MOTION by Mr. Green to approve New Business – Conditional Use 
Permit A26-0170, and to amend Condition #1 of the December 4th, 
2025, Approval to read as follows:  
 
Prior to the issuance of a Certificate of Occupancy, the Applicant 
shall have received final approval from the City of Nashua’s 
Engineering Department of the Division of Public Works for the 
design and reconstruction of the Pheasant Lane/Daniel Webster 
Highway intersection and shall post a financial security in a form 
approved by the City of Nashua and in an amount approved by the 
Engineering Department for all improvements. Said improvements 
shall be completed no sooner than March 15th, 2027, and no later  
than August 15th, 2027, and to the satisfaction of the Engineering 
Department. Such an amendment will be subject to the following 
subsequent condition: 
 
a. All prior conditions of approval from the September 7th, 2023, 
September 19th, 2024, and December 4 th, 2025 approvals are 
incorporated herein and made a part of this approval, unless 
superseded by a new condition. 
 
SECONDED by Ald. Klee 
 
MOTION CARRIED 6-0 
 
NEW BUSINESS – CONDITIONAL USE PERMITS 
A26-0164  C&J Properties, LLC (Owner), Kyle Cataldo (Appli cant) 
requesting conditional use approval of a vehicle repair 
and service business. Property is located at 444 Amherst 
Street. Map H – Lot 44. Zoned Park Industrial / Mixed 
Use (PI/MU). Ward 1. 
 
MOTION by Mr. Green that the application is complete and the 
Planning Board is ready to take jurisdiction 
 
SECONDED by Mr. Hirsch
NCPB 
September 17, 2026 
Page 12 
 
 
MOTION CARRIED 6-0 
 
Matthew Lara, Civil Engineer, TF Moran, 48 Constitution Dr, 
Bedford, NH 
 
Mr. Lara introduced himself on behalf of the applicant. We are 
seeking a conditional use perm it to convert the site to vehicle 
repair. The property is currently used as a photography studio, 
but previous to that it was used as a machine shop. It still has 
the infrastructure in place, there are two garage bays for 
conducting repairs. It has everything needed, we are not changing 
anything to the site. There may be some interior removal of plywood 
to the bays, façade upgrades, and some interior upgrades, but 
nothing structural. We are seeking a waiver, as detailed in the 
staff report. The most recent plan from 2022 shows the machine 
shop, and we would be going back to that.  
 
The Board had no further questions.  
 
SPEAKING IN OPPOSITION OR CONCERN 
 
None 
 
SPEAKING IN FAVOR 
 
None 
 
Mr. Varley said the waiver request is to not provide a site plan. 
What are we waiving, the submission of one? 
 
Mr. Durfee said correct.  
 
Ald. Klee said the engineering comment relative to traffic, can 
she get more insight? 
 
Mr. Hudson said we typically credit whatever the difference in 
existing traffic to proposed traffic. We re quest contribution to 
the traffic corridor based on the increase in trips, not the total. 
They are due a reduction of half based on the existing traffic. 
 
Ald. Klee said at one time there was a Walmart proposed at Building 
19, and there were concerns about automotive or hair salon because 
it abuts a conservation area. This is not too far from that. Is 
there an issue?
NCPB 
September 17, 2026 
Page 13 
 
Mr. Durfee said no, they are not triggering any wetland review 
from the Conservation Commission or Zoning Board. 
 
Mr. Hudson said Pennichuck Water has an overlay district for the 
water supply. They would do that approval with Pennichuck. It the 
use is internal to the building it may not be an issue.  
 
Ald. Klee said there is also a conservation area below that too. 
 
Mr. McPhie said that Pennichuck would usually address it.  
 
Mr. Varley confirmed that the applicant was amenable to paying the 
traffic corridor contribution fee.  
 
PUBLIC MEETING 
 
Mr. Varley closed the public hearing and opened the public meeting. 
He said this is a relatively straig htforward application with 
minimal impact on the site. It seems like a modest plan and a 
historical use as well.  
 
MOTION by Mr. Green to approve the following waivers for 
Conditional Use Permit A26-0164: 
 
a. §190-271: To waive the requirement to submit a site plan 
 
As per RSA 674:36(II)(N), RSA 674:44(III)(e), and §190 -148(D), 
Strict conformity would pose an unnecessary hardship to the 
Applicant and the waiver would not be contrary to the spirit and 
intent of the regulations; and specific circumstances, or 
conditions of the land, and the waiver will properly carry out the 
spirit and intent of the regulations. 
 
SECONDED by Mr. MacIntyre 
 
MOTION CARRIED 6-0 
 
MOTION by Mr. Green to approve New Business – Conditional Use 
Permit A26-0164. The Board finds that the a pplication meets the 
Approval Criteria under §190-133(F) with the following conditions: 
 
1. Prior to issuing the building permit, all comments in a memo 
from Joe Mendola, Senior Staff Engineer September 16, 2026, 
will be resolved to the satisfaction of the Division of Public 
Works. 
SECONDED by Mr. Hudson
NCPB 
September 17, 2026 
Page 14 
 
 
MOTION CARRIED 6-0 
 
NEW BUSINESS – SITE PLANS 
A26-0186  Northeastern SPE LLC (Owner and Applicant) requesting 
minor site plan amendment to place 36 self -storage 
containers on -site. Property is located at 111 
Northeastern Boulevard. Map 140 – Lot 1. Zoned Park 
Industrial (PI). Ward 6. 
 
MOTION by Mr. Green that the application is not a Development of 
Regional Impact 
 
SECONDED by Mr. Hirsch 
 
MOTION CARRIED 6-0 
 
MOTION by Mr. Green that the application is complete  and the 
Planning Board is ready to take jurisdiction 
 
SECONDED by Mr. Hirsch 
 
MOTION CARRIED 6-0 
 
Atty. Chris Swiniarski, Devine Millimet, 111 Amherst St, 
Manchester, NH 
 
Atty. Swiniarski introduced himself on behalf of the owner. As 
detailed in the staff report, we are asking to eliminate 36 parking 
spaces onsite for the placement of self -storage containers. 
Currently the site has 53 parking spaces, we will end up with 15 
spaces. There will be no physical change to the site, these parking 
spaces are not going to be removed, just occupied by storage units. 
There isn’t that much more to this. He feels this meets the waiver 
criteria. The use contemplated here does not require parking, there 
are 1-2 employees onsite and we still have 15 parking. Self-storage 
doesn’t require much parking beyond loading and unloading. This 
site was developed in 199 4 for mixed retail , o ffice, and 
warehousing. This is an adaptive reuse of the site  for a demand 
that the community needs.  
 
Atty. Swiniarski said this request is in connection to a 
contemplated sale of the property. Atty. Brad Westgate is here to 
represent the buyer, and is here to answer questions.
NCPB 
September 17, 2026 
Page 15 
 
Mr. Varley asked if the internal structure of the building is 
already used for self-storage.
